chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband dies while she is in the state of Ihram (for Hajj); does she perform Hajj? He said, 'Yes.'

The Shaykh (Al-Shaykh Al-Tusi) said, may Allah have mercy on him: And if a man makes walking upon himself the obligation to go to the House of Allah (the Exalted), and he becomes unable to do so, then let him ride, and there is no penalty upon him.

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: The one whose husband has died (referring to the widow)
key_terms.فَعَجَزَ عَنْهُ: And he became unable/incapable of it
key_terms.وَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: And there is no penalty/obligation upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman whose husband dies during Hajj, and does a walker incur a penalty if he rides instead?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies two practical rulings in Hajj jurisprudence: first, it confirms that a widow whose husband dies during the pilgrimage remains obligated to complete her own Hajj, and second, it establishes that a pilgrim who vows to walk but becomes physically unable may ride without incurring a penalty (kaffarah). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) and the removal of undue burden when circumstances change, aligning with the principle that vows are binding only as long as the capacity to fulfill them exists.
